fields.h1: Build a Job Posting Form That Clears HR Before It Goes Live
fields.hero_description: Build a job posting form that collects each opening's title, pay range, and close date, and holds it until HR approves.
fields.features_heading: What a Posting Needs Before Anyone Sees It
fields.features_subheading: A job posting form is the request behind a public listing. Emergent builds its fields and its sign-off, plus a table of open roles.
fields.feature_1:
Pay range as two numbers, not a sentence

The form asks for a low and a high figure and whether the pay is hourly or yearly. A request with the high figure below the low one goes back to the manager before HR ever opens it.
fields.feature_2:
Sign-off before the posting goes public

Each request waits for the approver you name, such as HR or a department head. They get an email or a Slack message, approve it or return it with a note, and the decision is saved.
fields.feature_3:
Location and schedule picked from a list

Managers choose the clinic, store, or campus, then the schedule: full time, part time, or seasonal. Each pick becomes a filter on the careers page and a column in the postings table.
fields.feature_4:
A close date on every posting

Ask for the date applications stop. On that date the app takes the posting down and marks it closed, unless the manager extends it first, and the request keeps its full history.
fields.feature_5:
Every posting is a row you own

Requests, approvals, and close dates sit in a database you own, not in a vendor's account. Filter by department to see what each manager has open and how long approval took.
fields.feature_6:
Export the code to your GitHub

On paid plans, export the full codebase to your GitHub repository when postings need to feed an applicant tracking system you already run, then keep building on it there.

fields.tab_content_1:
No vet tech posting goes live before HR signs the pay range

Ines Vardanyan runs one of the 6 Kestrel Pine Veterinary clinics and needs a vet tech. She fills in the job posting form: the title, the Eastgate clinic, full time, $19 to $23 an hour, and a close date of Dec 4. HR director Pernell Asquith gets an email and approves the range. Only then does the posting go on the careers page.
fields.tab_content_2:
30-day listings that an editor reads first

Employers post seasonal and year-round jobs on Fenwick Trails Jobs, a board for outdoor work, through its submission form. Each listing names the company, the role, the location, and the pay range. Marisol Tran reads every one before it appears on the board, and an approved listing runs for 30 days.
fields.tab_content_3:
Three internships wait, each with its pay field blank

Calder Valley's career office collects internship postings from local employers through one form. This week 14 came in. The office approved 11, and the 3 that left pay blank went back to their employers with a note asking for an hourly rate, or a mark that the role is unpaid.
fields.tab_content_4:
Every posting past 45 days goes to Lucan

Twelve roles are open across the 9 Marlowe Hardware stores, each one a row with its store and the days it has been open. Any posting open more than 45 days goes to Lucan Thibault, the recruiter, in a Slack direct message. Today that is 2: a cashier in Fairmount and a yard lead in Brookside.

fields.howto_title: How to Create a Job Posting Form
fields.howto_description: Seven steps to build a job posting form that gets each opening approved before it posts and closes it on time.
fields.howto_step_1_title: 01 Start from the roles you post most
fields.howto_step_2_title: 02 Ask for what the public listing shows
fields.howto_step_4_title: 04 Describe the form in plain English
fields.howto_step_1_des: Pull last year's openings and sort them into groups, such as hourly store roles and internships. Give each group its own questions. A cashier request should never ask about a relocation package.
fields.howto_step_2_des: Collect the title, location, schedule, pay, and a short description of the work. Keep internal details like the budget code in a separate section that never reaches the careers page.
fields.howto_step_3_des: Pick the approver for each kind of request: HR for pay, a department head for headcount. When an approver returns a request, the manager edits that same request with the note attached, not a fresh one.
fields.howto_step_4_des: Write a few sentences for Emergent: who fills the form in, the fields, the approver, and where an approved posting goes. Emergent builds the form and the database behind it, and you change either one by prompting.
fields.howto_step_5_title: 05 Set what the close date does
fields.howto_step_5_des: Choose what the app does when applications stop: take the posting down, or ask the manager whether to extend it. Set one default for every role, and no posting runs without an end date.
fields.howto_step_6_des: Send a request with the pay figures reversed and no close date, and check that it goes back to the manager. Then approve a clean request and find it on the careers page.
fields.howto_step_7_title: 07 Send the form link to your managers
fields.howto_step_7_des: Share the link with everyone who opens roles and retire the email thread they used before. After the first week of requests, add any field the managers kept typing into the description.

faq_plan.q: What is a job posting form?
faq_plan.a: A job posting form is the form an employer fills in to open a role before the listing goes public. It records the role, where and when the work happens, what it pays, and when applications stop. It can work as an internal request that HR approves, or as the submission form a job board takes listings through.

faq_plan.q: How do I create a job posting form?
faq_plan.a: Start a prompt in Emergent's AI form builder with the roles you post and the person who approves them. For example: "Build a job posting form for my 3 restaurants that sends each request to my HR lead." Emergent builds the form and its database from that sentence. The free tier covers building and publishing.

faq_plan.q: What fields belong in a job posting form template?
faq_plan.a: Cover the six facts a public listing shows: job title, location, schedule, pay, a description of the work, and the date applications close. A job posting form template for internal requests adds the department, the hiring manager, and the person who approves the role.

faq_plan.q: Does the employer or the candidate fill in a job posting form?
faq_plan.a: The employer does. A manager or a recruiter fills in the job posting form to open the role, and a candidate fills in a job application form once the listing is live. Keep the two apart: one records the opening, and the other records each person who applies to it.

faq_plan.q: Who should approve a request sent through a job posting form?
faq_plan.a: Have one person approve the pay and one approve the wording, or one person for both on a small team. Pick the pay approver by who owns the budget for the role. In a form built on Emergent, the app reminds that approver when a request sits for two days.

faq_plan.q: Can a job posting form track how long each posting has been open?
faq_plan.a: Yes. Record the day each posting went live and have the app count the days since. Sort the open postings by that count every Monday. Ask the manager of anything near the top whether the role is still needed, or whether its pay or title should change.

faq_plan.q: What comes after the close date on a job posting form?
faq_plan.a: Applicant review comes next. Shortlist the people who applied before the close date and interview them. Before an offer, send a reference check form to the references your top candidate lists, and keep the posting's row open until the role is filled.

faq_plan.q: What wording should a job posting form flag before a listing goes live?
faq_plan.a: Flag wording that prefers one sex or race, or that puts off applicants 40 or older. The EEOC says it is illegal to publish a job ad that shows a preference for or discourages applicants because of race, color, religion, sex, national origin, age (40 or older), disability, or genetic information. Its example is an ad seeking recent college graduates, which may discourage people over 40.

faq_plan.q: Can a job posting form publish approved jobs to a careers page?
faq_plan.a: Yes. The app Emergent builds can list every approved posting on a careers page and take each one down on its close date. Built apps also connect to any tool with an API, and postings can sync to the applicant tracking system you already use.

faq_plan.q: What should a job posting form record once the role is filled?
faq_plan.a: Record the date the role was filled and the hire's start date on the posting's row, and take the listing down the same day. Every day it stays up, it can collect applications for a job that is gone. The person you hired then fills in a new employee form, and the posting's row keeps the dates it opened and closed.

plan.angle: No live top 10 for this Wave 3 keyword, and every AlsoAsked question drifts to job-seeker advice. The searcher who wants a job posting form is the employer side: a hiring manager asking HR to open a role, a job board taking listings from employers, or a career office collecting internships. This page builds that intake form: the fields a posting needs before it goes public (title, location, pay range, description, close date), an approval step before anything is posted, and a table of every open posting with its age, so a listing filled last month does not stay up.
